blocks.response_text: At 16:54:20 [reported] the control room initiated instructions to generation to restore the system frequency and response levels. In total 1,240 MW [reported] of actions were taken, using Short Term Operating Reserve, Rapid Start, Balancing Mechanism actions and Fast Reserve. They included rapid start of one Dinorwig unit, instructions to another Dinorwig unit and two Ffestiniog units from a synchronising position to generating, an additional distribution-connected diesel generator and 400 MW [reported] of short term operating reserve. Coryton South and Carrington were instructed to cover the enduring loss of generation.

blocks.response_text: The first report of demand disconnection from a DNO reached the control room at 16:56 [reported]. blocks.response_text: We instructed the DNOs to restore demand progressively from 16:58 to 17:16 [reported]. The DNOs did ask our specific permission to restore. blocks.response_text: Our technical report records that we told the NGET control room at 17:32 [reported] that DNOs had started restoration. Our earlier answers to the E3C, based on the data we had on 28 August 2019, gave 17:22 [reported] for that message.

blocks.response_text: Most distribution-connected generation gives us no indication of its proposed output and no actual output data. Our estimate of approximately 500 MW [estimated] of embedded generation lost came from the change in metered flows between the transmission and distribution networks in our IEMS system, corrected for the frequency characteristics of demand and for frequency response services in the distribution network.

provenance.quote: We also secure the system to within a ROCOF limit of 0.125 Hz/s for the largest credible loss.
provenance.section: Appendix M – ESO E3C Questions and Answers (data available to the ESO on 28 August 2019), answer 11

provenance.quote: We also consider the impact of vector shift protection on embedded generation where appropriate to do so.
provenance.section: Appendix M – ESO E3C Questions and Answers (data available to the ESO on 28 August 2019), answer 11

provenance.quote: Approximately 2 GW of small generators are connected to the distribution networks via relays which disconnect the generators if the RoCoF is greater than 0.125Hz/s.
provenance.section: Appendix H – Managing Frequency with Statutory Limits

provenance.quote: Approximately 8.5 GW of small generators are connected to the distribution networks via relays which disconnect the generators if the Vector Shift angle is greater than 6 degrees.
provenance.section: Appendix H – Managing Frequency with Statutory Limits

blocks.response_text: We secure the system to within a RoCoF limit of 0.125 Hz/s [reported] for the largest credible loss. Approximately 2 GW [reported] of small generators are on relays that disconnect above 0.125 Hz/s [reported], and approximately 8.5 GW [reported] on relays that disconnect for a vector shift angle greater than 6 degrees [reported]. We also consider the impact of vector shift protection on embedded generation where appropriate.

provenance.quote: The ESO does not currently measure system inertia directly but instead estimates it using a model. The inertia estimate is derived from the forecasted demand level, embedded solar and wind
provenance.section: Appendix M – ESO E3C Questions and Answers (data available to the ESO on 28 August 2019), answer 42

blocks.response_text: We do not currently measure system inertia directly; we estimate it with a model, derived from the forecast demand level and embedded solar and wind.

blocks.response_text: Where a large infeed loss is more likely to come with significant vector shift protection losses, we manage for that event too, even though this is strictly not within the requirements of the security standards.
